question: Does late night eating impair concentration?

provenance.study: SLEEP 2015 conference presentation - Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania
provenance.citation: Spaeth AM, Dinges DF, Goel N. Presented at SLEEP 2015 (29th Annual Meeting of the Associated Professional Sleep Societies), Seattle WA, June 6-10, 2015. Lock5 3e cites: University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine. 'Eating less during late night hours may stave off some effects of sleep deprivation.' ScienceDaily, June 4, 2015.
provenance.design: Randomized experiment: 44 adults aged 21-50, 4 h sleep/night for 3 nights, night-4 randomization to continued food access (n=20) vs water-only from 10 pm (n=24); 2 a.m. testing nightly.
provenance.data_source: No Lock5 dataset (3e data page checked Oct 2026). data/phase2/q16_latenight.csv is a documented reconstruction (seed 2026) calibrated to the published direction of effects and PVT magnitudes typical of 4 h time in bed; per-participant values are synthetic.
provenance.caution: Published findings are qualitative (no group means/SDs released); the numeric results here illustrate the analysis pipeline for this design.

decision.question: Does late night eating impair concentration?
decision.verdict: Yes - in this randomized experiment, the group kept awake with late-night food access had significantly slower reaction times and more attention lapses on night 4 than the group fasted from 10 pm; the eaters also declined significantly from their nights 1-3 level, while the fasting group did not decline.
decision.causality: Randomization of the night-4 condition supports a causal conclusion: late-night eating (vs fasting) worsens some effects of sleep restriction on vigilant attention.
decision.scope: Conclusions are about vigilance under acute sleep restriction (4 h/night); per-participant values in the CSV are a documented reconstruction, so numeric p-values illustrate the pipeline rather than replicate the unpublished study statistics.
